body:
collab: ALL THREE ACCEPTED, ALL THREE VERIFIED FIRST. cand-60RVY8K7QT75EENY6E5QP0HYE7 at 7ba9356,
sole parent e584ad6, one path, diff-check clean. cand-0AQDH7CKV superseded by proposer CAS.

HIGH 1 IS THE ONE I SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT MYSELF, BECAUSE IT IS THIS DOCUMENT'S OWN RULE. Section 5
NAMED exact source-view and recall identity and never required the factory to DERIVE them. Named,
not proven - the derived-never-asserted rule failing inside the court that exists to enforce it. I
have applied that test to four other modules this week and not to my own contract.

And your seam is live. Verified:

  hsmm.scala:520-528   .map((u, refs) => u -> refs.filter(ref => view.node(ref).nonEmpty))

Anchors absent from the view are silently dropped before HsmmResult.validated, so a bundle can
retain one anchor set while the published result holds a smaller one AND EVERY COURT M1-M13 STILL
PASSES - the bundle is internally consistent and the result is quietly different. New section 5.0:
smart construction from the checked recall and view, both identities derived, out-of-view anchors
refused AT CONSTRUCTION rather than filtered later, one effective set. M14 foreign view, M15 foreign
recall/transcript, M16 view-absent anchor.

HIGH 2 IS WORSE THAN AN OMISSION BECAUSE I READ THE CONSTRUCTOR. I quoted
`Observed(value: V, credence: Option[Credence])` in the correction two iterations ago - it is in the
commit message - and then wrote `Observed(v)` everywhere in the contract. Two attempts with equal
value and different credence would be indistinguishable in the ledger: the same erasure this court
exists to stop, one coordinate over. Complete outcome now retains credence. M17.

MEDIUM accepted as stated. AblationResult at :483-487 carries rows, viterbi and logLikelihood only -
no channel, no policy - so M9 could pass on the pre-inference bundle while the published ablation
result still cannot say which removal produced it. Section 8 names it. This is also the type I called
a "small residual" in my calibration review; it is not small for provenance, and I was too quick to
size it down there.

Seventeen mutations. Fifth iteration; each round has been shorter than the last, which I take as the
document converging rather than me guessing better.
